correctness.rationale: Writing the bracket into a fixed generator z of [L,L] gives a scalar bilinear form. For each fixed first argument, reciprocity gives identical kernels of the two linear functionals, so both are zero or proportional. Linearity on sums with independent images makes the scalar constant when image rank is at least two, and in rank one it is constant on the common one-dimensional quotient by the row and column map kernels. Transposing shows the constant is ±1, yielding the dichotomy in odd characteristic. In the non-Lie case a nonzero square spans [L,L], and the right Leibniz identity annihilates squares on the right; reciprocity then makes the line central. For a noncentral Lie law with b(x,z)=phi(x), choosing h with phi(h)=1 shows from Jacobi that b vanishes on ker(phi)×ker(phi); the kernel there of b(h,-) is central and complements Kz. This gives aff_1 plus an abelian summand and b=phi∧alpha with alpha(z)=1. For each phi nonzero annihilating z, alpha has q^(n−1) choices before quotienting by alpha→alpha+t phi, hence q^(n−2) distinct b. Central forms are counted on the quotient of dimension n−1, without dividing labelled laws by scalar rescalings once a generator has been fixed. Up to scalar congruence the symmetric determinant-square classes coalesce only in odd rank; alternating forms have one class per nonzero even rank. These yield the exact two count formulas, including n=2. The boundary example has central outputs and reversed coordinate pair (ac,−(ad−bc)), which proves reciprocity, and its nonzero square and nonzero antisymmetric part distinguish it from both branches. Independent replay: python3 /workspace/reproductions/audit_leibniz.py exhausts every nonzero scalar matrix at a fixed derived line over F3 for n=2 and n=3, tests the identity and reciprocity, and then enumerates isomorphism orbits under the line stabilizer. This gives 16 and 676 labelled laws across all lines and 2 and 5 isomorphism classes, respectively. These finite verifications are not the arbitrary-field proof.
residual_risks: Odd characteristic is essential for disjoint symmetric and alternating nonzero families in the argument.
The smooth real rack interpretation is not a finite-field assertion.

evidence: The nonnilpotent non-Lie classification is stated for left Leibniz; taking the opposite gives the right convention, and its one-sided nonzero product excludes reciprocity. The isotopy paper explicitly recalls the older isomorphism normal forms of indecomposable nilpotent rank-one-derived algebras. Demir et al. use a complement of the derived line and a scalar form for central two-step cases in their complex bounded-dimension setting.
broader_coverage.reasoning: These sources supply important structural coverage, including more than just isotopy in the background literature. They do not supply a count of distinct coordinate laws on a fixed n-space obeying reciprocity over every odd finite field. Such a count requires treating the disjoint branches and parameter redundancies, not just naming abstract isomorphism types.

evidence: The sign dichotomy is known by scalar reflexivity, and the isomorphism tally is a straightforward aggregate after reduction to symmetric and alternating forms. A count of labelled laws additionally evaluates the number on each derived line, notably q^(n−2)(q^(n−1)−1) for the noncentral branch, and controls overcounting. The compared scalar/rank-one results do not assert a sharp derived-dimension-two counterexample or the labelled formula.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Credit the mechanically covered structural portions. The exact fixed-space count is a further finite-field enumeration for the natural Noether-motivated condition, not a direct specialization of a prior numerical formula or census.

originality.rationale: Pass is for the integrated reciprocity-selected exact census, especially the all-dimension labelled census, with an explicit sharp boundary example. The rank-one symmetric/alternating implication itself is a direct application of scalar form reflexivity; the nilpotent bilinear-form classification and the ordinary finite-field congruence inputs are also prior. No originality is assigned to those ingredients or to formulating reciprocity as a real Noether criterion.
residual_risks: Older rank-one form classifications may support other derivations of parts of the tally. No claim is made that the finite-field similarity rules, affine Lie classification, or scalar reflexivity are new.

value.rationale: Counting the coordinate laws satisfying a motivated algebraic zero-product condition gives a usable exact finite-field benchmark, not just a list of abstract algebras. In particular the count separates three families with very different parameter multiplicities while the isomorphism tally is independent of the odd field size. The rank-two example exhibits the exact failure of using the rank-one conclusion to infer bracket symmetry from reciprocal zeros at larger derived dimension.
residual_risks: This value is in the selected census and boundary, not in a claim of new general bilinear-form theory or a finite-field smooth rack characterization.
